summary.goal: Implement dynamic specialists that are spawned on-demand by the Interviewer. Specialists contribute freeform observations - intelligence lives in their prompts, not schema constraints. User never sees specialists - they're invisible infrastructure.
in_scope: Prompt templates for common specialist types (Architect, DataModeller, Designer, QA, Security)
Freeform observation contribution via MCP tools
Specialist-to-specialist awareness (can see each other's observations)
out_of_scope: Fixed specialist roles (Interviewer decides what to spawn)

acceptance_criteria.description: Prompt templates for common specialist types (suggestions, not requirements)
Specialists are spawned LAZILY by Interviewer when expertise is needed
Specialists join session channel via Relay and observe conversation
Specialists use update_observations MCP tool with freeform Record<string, unknown>
Observations structure is defined by specialist prompt, not enforced by schema
Specialists can read other specialists' observations via read_understanding tool
Specialists queue insights for Interviewer (never speak to user directly)
Interviewer spawns specialists with custom focus/prompt based on conversation needs
Specialists are released when session is abandoned

decisions.rationale: Interviewer spawns specialists on-demand based on conversation needs. More efficient, allows dynamic specialist types.
Intelligence lives in agent prompts, not Zod schemas. Any structure that makes sense for the specialist's domain.
User sees only Interviewer. Specialists contribute insights that Interviewer weaves into conversation.
Common templates (Architect, Designer, etc.) as suggestions. Interviewer can spawn custom specialists as needed.

summary.notes: Specialists are 'wise observers' not 'task workers'. They watch, notice patterns, raise concerns, and contribute understanding. They never appear in the user conversation - Interviewer facilitates and presents insights as its own.

steps.title: Create specialist prompt templates
steps.description: Create prompt templates for common specialist types (suggestions, not requirements)

acceptance_criteria.description: SPECIALIST_TEMPLATES: Map<string, { displayName, focus, basePrompt }>
Templates for: Architect (system design), DataModeller (schemas), Designer (UX), QA (testing), Security
Templates are suggestions - Interviewer can spawn custom specialists with inline prompts
getSpecialistPrompt(name, focus, customContext?) builds complete prompt

steps.title: Define specialist MCP tools
steps.description: Create MCP tool definitions for specialist capabilities (freeform observations)

acceptance_criteria.description: update_observations: { session_id, observations: Record<string, unknown> } -> freeform observations
read_understanding: { session_id } -> returns all specialists' observations
queue_insight: { session_id, type: 'question'|'observation'|'concern', content, priority } -> queues for Interviewer
Observations structure is NOT validated - intelligence lives in prompts

steps.title: Implement specialist tool execution
steps.description: Create MCP tool handlers for specialist tools

acceptance_criteria.description: executeSpecialistTool(specialistName, toolName, input, storage) dispatches to handler
update_observations calls storage.updateUnderstanding(sessionId, specialistName, observations)
read_understanding calls storage.getSession() and returns full understanding
queue_insight calls queueSpecialistInput() from Interviewer module

steps.title: Implement specialist release
steps.description: Release specialists when session is abandoned

acceptance_criteria.description: releaseSpecialists(sessionId) releases all spawned specialists for session
Reads session.active_specialists[] to find agent IDs
Uses Relay release() for each agent
Called when session status changes to 'abandoned'
